headline: A sunny but cool Saturday gives way to light rain Sunday evening in Los Angeles County, but the bigger story is a significant coastal flooding threat Thanksgiving week from very high tides and a large incoming swell.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Saturday is mostly sunny after a chilly start; the interior Frost Advisory expires at 9 AM and patchy low clouds well to the northwest clear by late morning. North to northeast winds gusting 25 to 40 mph across the mountains and valleys this morning stay below advisory levels and die down this afternoon. Despite the sunshine, highs only reach the 60s in the Glendale area and elsewhere west of the mountains and the mid to upper 50s farther inland, about 4 to 8 degrees below normal. Saturday night stays dry.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: A weak cold front brings rain to most areas Sunday, reaching San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara counties in the afternoon and Ventura and Los Angeles counties in the evening. Amounts are light: up to a quarter inch on the Central Coast, maybe a tenth of an inch in the Los Angeles area, and less than a tenth inland, with southerly winds ahead of the front warming things a degree or two. Monday is sunny and warmer, with highs in the mid 60s to lower 70s at the coast and in the valleys, and a morning push of northerly winds off the land brings gusts below advisory levels through and below north-south passes and canyons.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Tuesday stays dry but grows cloudier as the next weak storm approaches, with coast and valley highs in the upper 60s to lower 70s, about 2 to 4 degrees below normal. Rain arrives Tuesday night and ends by early Wednesday afternoon, with only a 20–30% chance south of Point Conception, including the Los Angeles area, and under a tenth of an inch if any; coastal San Luis Obispo County has a better than 70% chance (about 50% elsewhere on the Central Coast) and up to half an inch north of Morro Bay. Thanksgiving and Black Friday are sunny, dry and warmer as high pressure builds, with possibly enough wind off the land for a moderate wind event; highs warm about 6 degrees on Thanksgiving and another 2 to 4 on Friday, reaching the 70s at all coasts and valleys, 5 to 10 degrees above normal.

coast: Forecasters have significant concern for moderate to major coastal flooding Thanksgiving week from a combination of unusually high sea levels from warm ocean water, very high spring tides, and a large long-period west swell. For the Central Coast, Ventura and Los Angeles counties, a Coastal Flood Advisory runs from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM Wednesday, followed by a Coastal Flood Watch from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon; peak high tides between 8:45 and 10 AM are predicted around 8.2–8.6 feet in Los Angeles and Ventura and 7.9–8.2 feet on the Central Coast, with a reasonable worst case 0.3–0.5 feet higher. If upgraded to a warning, impacts could include damaging flooding of coastal roads and structures and significant beach erosion; areas of greatest concern include Santa Monica to Palos Verdes, Long Beach/Naples, Ventura Harbor and Faria to Silver Strand Beach, and Morro Bay, Pismo Beach and Oceano Dunes. The Santa Barbara South Coast and the islands are under a Coastal Flood Advisory from 3 AM Monday to 3 PM Thursday, with elevated to high surf likely all week and more coastal alerts likely for Friday. Offshore, winds and seas stay below small craft advisory levels through the weekend; a significant west swell around 14–16 feet arrives midweek with hazardous seas in the outer waters, and low-end advisory-level northwest to west winds are possible Wednesday and Wednesday night south of Point Conception.
watch_for: Coastal flooding Wednesday–Thursday mornings at high tide, which could be upgraded to a Coastal Flood Warning; stay off rock jetties and flooded roads.
Light rain Sunday evening in Los Angeles County, around a tenth of an inch.
A possible moderate offshore wind event on Thanksgiving and Friday.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the sunny, cool Saturday and light Sunday rain, fairly confident in a weak midweek storm and a warm, dry Thanksgiving, with how the swell and high tides line up the main uncertainty for coastal flooding.
